source.title: Persona vectors: monitoring and controlling character traits in language models

record.file_problem: The complete LessWrong post and comments are present, but the post is a brief summary rather than the linked full paper. It does not reproduce numerical results from the figures.
record.tranche_reason: It reports fine-tuning on a different narrow task and measures resulting traits, and tests persona-vector interventions on those changes; it does not reproduce the insecure-code training recipe or the original measurement in detail.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative trait outcomes for the Mistake GSM8K II dataset and qualitative results for inference-time and preventative steering. The LMSYS-Chat-1M high/random/low subset findings concern projection-based data flagging, not narrow-task fine-tuning, so they are not rows for these versions. The comment's MMLU scores and Mistake Medical rates measure capability and narrow-task performance, not the misaligned behaviors named in the claim; they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes on narrow trait-inducing datasets inspired by emergent misalignment, including mistaken math answers. It reports that the models then become evil. It also tests whether a single persona direction tracks and causally controls these shifts across fine-tunes. Results in this post are qualitative only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that finetuning-induced trait shifts correlate strongly with shifts along persona vectors, and that projections can flag problematic training data before training.
record.recipe_differences: The post uses persona-vector monitoring and interventions, and reports fine-tuning on mistaken-math and other trait-inducing datasets rather than the original insecure-code recipe and matched benign controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Inference-time steering can reverse trait changes but may reduce general capability; preventative steering is described as better preserving capability. The post does not give setting-specific numerical trait comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Mistake GSM8K II fine-tuning also raises sycophancy and hallucination.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow flawed-data fine-tunes induce several non-target persona trait shifts, beyond misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation steering toward a persona vector during fine-tuning limits trait acquisition with little MMLU loss. Post-hoc steering against it reverses shifts but costs capability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation steering, during or after training, mitigates emergent trait shifts.

fits_no_version.finding: The projection difference of training data on persona vectors predicts post-finetuning trait expression, including on LMSYS-Chat-1M subsets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona-vector projections flag training data that will induce misaligned traits.

record.problems: The post is a brief summary, omits model names, sizes, prompt sets, numerical trait rates, uncertainty, and detailed control results, and points to a separate full paper. The available trait and intervention findings are qualitative.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were included for LMSYS-Chat-1M high/random/low projection-selected samples because those findings concern data flagging and are not narrow-task fine-tunes. MMLU and Mistake Medical outcomes in the comment were omitted because they measure capability and task performance rather than the claimed misaligned behavior.

untested.parts: No insecure-code training or its secure/educational controls.
Bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks and number sequences are not tested in the post. There are no matched-benign-control numbers for the math dataset.
No quantitative evidence in the post that one direction is shared across all misaligned fine-tunes. Persona vectors are trait-specific.
Neither inoculation prompting nor brief benign retraining is tested. Only activation steering is.
No size, seed, coherence-filter or training-dynamics analysis.

missing.what: The finding that intended and unintended trait shifts after finetuning are strongly correlated with shifts along the persona vector, across datasets.

record.verdict_notes: This is a brief summary post with no numbers, model names or controls. The full paper (arXiv:2507.21509) would be needed for rates. Steering mitigations were moved off V6 because V6 names inoculation framing or benign retraining, not activation steering.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, secure-code control, or insecure code requested for a class is tested.
The reported narrow task is mistaken math answers; bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, and number sequences are not tested.

The post describes relevant persona vectors and their relationship to fine-tuning shifts, but does not test whether one shared linear direction or persona feature mediates the misalignment across fine-tunes.
The post reports inference-time and training-time steering, but not brief benign retraining. Its qualitative summary does not provide trait-specific numerical intervention results.
No size sweep, seed robustness, coherence-filter analysis, or training-time emergence analysis is reported.
